newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - GOLD UP, SILVER STABLE, PLATINUM CHOPPY.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - GOLD UP, SILVER STABLE, PLATINUM CHOPPY.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold is likely to trade towards the higher end of its $321.00/$328.00 range on Monday against the backdrop of falling stock prices and a recent easing in the dollar, traders and chartists said.
Silver is expected to consolidate around $4.40, while platinum and palladium look set for another week of choppy and nervous trading, they added.
GOLD - Despite Far Eastern profit-taking, gold is expected to probe towards the higher end of its $321.00/$328.00 an ounce range, traders said on Monday.
Support was likely to be found from declining stocks and the recent easing in the dollar.
But traders said any substantial gains could be short-lived as they expected producer selling to emerge. "Overall the market remains in a bearish mode," one trader commented.
The FTSE 100 opened 1.13 percent or 56.5 points lower after the DOW fell further on Friday following the London close.
In early European trading the dollar was down from overnight highs.
Traders said they did not expect prices to break above $328.00.
"There is a lack of robust buying in the market; if anything sellers may be tempted to liquidate on moves towards $327.00 and $328.00," the trader said.
At 0730 GMT spot gold was quoted at $326.40/326.90, against Friday's London close of $324.60/$325.10.

SILVER - Seen consolidating around $4.40, with support and resistance roughly pegged at $4.30 and $4.50. Referring to the Comex September silver contract, Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff said, "Continues the uptrend...with the technical indicators continuing to point up."
"Before becoming too confident the market requires a breach of $4.52 and then $4.57 to confirm the uptrend," Squires added.
At 0730 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.39/4.41, little changed.
PLATINUM - Meanwhile, the PGMs looked set for another week of volatile trading.

"The PGM metals continue to be concerned with the large open position on Tocom. While they have fallen from an estimated 50 tonnes of palladium in July, they are still believed to be a heady 30 tonnes," GNI said in its commodity report.

Traders said PGMs remained physically tight following the recent suspension of shipments from producer Russia for six months. Despite a resumption of Russian shipments, traders said the market was still short.
"Our view is that the Russians are not going to bail this market out," Flemings Global Mining Group said.

"If this assumption is correct, tightness could continue until either the funds holding material release it to the markets, or demand adjusts itself to the new and lower levels of supply," Flemings added.
At 0730 GMT spot platinum was quoted at $443.50/446.50, versus $442.00/$445.00.
